sources.title: Telecommunications Market Data Update — Q1 2026
facts: 29.4 million fixed broadband lines at end-Q1 2026
Fixed broadband lines increased by 282,000 (1.0%) year-on-year
Dedicated mobile broadband subscriptions reached 5.2 million
Mobile data usage reached 3,042 PB, up 13.1% year-on-year
limitations: Market totals are not premises coverage or live orderability
Quarterly aggregates cannot be assigned to a parcel

sources.title: Broadband complaints fall to record low
facts: Q1 2026 broadband complaints were six per 100,000 customers
The reported rate was the lowest in Ofcom's series
TalkTalk generated the most broadband complaints in the provider comparison
Plusnet and Sky generated the fewest fixed broadband complaints
limitations: Complaints measure service experience, not network coverage
Provider rankings are quarter-specific and relative to customer bases

sources.title: Social tariffs: Cheaper broadband and phone packages
sources.evidence_kind: current affordability guidance and tariff listing
facts: Listed social-tariff prices range from £10 to £24
Most listed tariffs offer speeds above 30 Mbit/s
Eligibility commonly includes Universal Credit and Pension Credit
Provider availability and qualifying benefits vary by tariff
limitations: Tariff listing does not prove availability at a specific address
Current provider eligibility must be checked before use

sources.title: Broadband and mobile coverage checker
sources.evidence_kind: postcode coverage-checker and developer API guidance
sources.geography: United Kingdom postcode and interactive-map views
facts: Checker reports standard, superfast and ultrafast broadband availability
Mobile coverage can be viewed by provider
Fixed broadband and mobile data APIs are available
Checker does not report maintenance or local network incidents
limitations: Predicted checker output is not live provider orderability
Checker limitations must remain visible in parcel gating
sources.licence: Ofcom official HTML and API terms link; attribution retained

sources.title: Your right to request a decent broadband service
sources.geography: United Kingdom; BT and KCOM service areas
facts: Decent connection threshold is at least 10 Mbit/s down and 1 Mbit/s up
Eligibility excludes premises due to receive a public scheme within 12 months
BT or KCOM has 30 days to confirm eligibility and build cost
Network build cost up to £3,400 is not charged to the applicant
limitations: Legal request eligibility is not current service availability
Price and cost thresholds require current source revalidation

sources.title: Broadband speeds: what you need to know
facts: Participating providers must provide a minimum guaranteed speed
Unfixed provider-network speed problems after 30 days can trigger penalty-free exit
Peak-time estimates use 8–10pm for homes and 12–2pm for businesses
Ethernet testing is recommended because Wi-Fi can reduce measured speed
limitations: Contractual speed protection is not coverage evidence
Provider participation and contract terms must be checked

sources.title: Codes of practice
sources.evidence_kind: complaints, ADR, automatic-compensation and speed-code index
facts: General Condition C4 requires compliant complaints procedures
Providers must belong to an approved ADR scheme
Automatic compensation covers delayed repairs, missed appointments and delayed starts for signatories
Updated broadband speed codes apply to purchases from 21 December 2022
limitations: Code membership does not prove local network quality or coverage
Signatory lists may change and require dated revalidation

sources.title: Switching mobile, broadband or landline
facts: Broadband and landline switching can use One Touch Switch
The new provider can arrange the broadband or landline switch
Mobile switching can use Text to Switch
Separate guidance exists when a provider ceases trading
limitations: Switching process does not prove service availability
Retail process and address eligibility remain separate

sources.title: How to get more from your broadband
sources.evidence_kind: postcode prediction and consumer decision guidance
facts: Checker results are the fastest predicted speeds supplied by network operators
Actual property availability and received speeds may differ
Standard is below 30 Mbit/s, superfast 30–300 Mbit/s, ultrafast above 300 Mbit/s
Unresolved complaints can proceed to ADR after eight weeks or deadlock
limitations: Predicted highest speeds are not guaranteed packages
Postcode results cannot be promoted without provider confirmation

sources.title: Gigabit Broadband Voucher Scheme information
sources.geography: Open voucher areas in the United Kingdom
facts: Eligible homes and businesses may access vouchers up to £4,500
Scheme excludes areas with a Project Gigabit contract or planned commercial coverage
Projects require at least two eligible premises
New connections must meet specified improvement thresholds
limitations: Indicative eligibility is not a confirmed voucher award
Supplier and GBVS checks are required for an address
sources.licence: Crown copyright 2026; OGL v3.0 where stated

sources.title: Project Gigabit National Rolling Open Market Review May 2026
sources.evidence_kind: national commercial coverage and plan review
facts: May 2026 review formally closed on 1 June 2026
Review identifies where gigabit infrastructure exists or is planned over three years
National Rolling OMR occurs in January, May and September
Outcome and request-for-information documents are separated
limitations: Supplier plans are not completed build or live service
Review classification must not be treated as parcel orderability

sources.title: Project Gigabit Evaluation Plan
facts: Evaluation covers Gigabit Infrastructure Subsidy and voucher interventions
GIS uses subsidy contracts for non-commercial premises
Gigabit-capable is described as at least 1,000 Mbps download
GigaHubs are evaluated separately from this plan
limitations: Evaluation design is not delivery or coverage evidence
Programme mechanism cannot be assigned to a parcel

sources.title: Project Gigabit framework agreement – Openreach
facts: BDUK reports eight awarded call-off contracts under the framework
Framework targets hard-to-reach premises outside supplier commercial rollout
First listed call-off covers 60,180 contracted premises
First listed call-off contract value is £159.3 million
limitations: Contracted premises are not current built or orderable premises
Call-off totals cannot be assigned to a parcel without contract data and provider verification

sources.title: Data downloads 2025
sources.evidence_location: visible data table and related-content section
sources.geography: United Kingdom and published subnational files
facts: Fixed broadband coverage and full-fibre take-up downloads are listed
Fixed broadband performance downloads are listed
Mobile coverage downloads are listed
Data supports year-on-year infrastructure comparison
limitations: Dataset vintage is 2025 and must remain dated
Download index alone does not prove a current parcel value
sources.licence: Ofcom official page and linked terms; attribution retained

sources.title: Connected Nations FAQs
sources.evidence_location: visible FAQ on download types and 2024 methodology revision
facts: Since 2020 fixed coverage, fixed performance and mobile downloads are distinct
Speed information is available only for fixed broadband files
Collection methodology changed from July 2024
Ofcom considers average download speeds robust to local-authority level, not postcode level
limitations: Methodology guidance limits precision rather than supplying parcel values
Postcode-level performance inference is explicitly constrained
